title: Second-ideal quotient systems are annihilated by the thickening ideal
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I and K quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, M a coherent I-adic formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and e ≥ 0. Every term M_n/K^(e+1)M_n, using the recursive module quotient of that definition, is annihilated by the kernel ideal of the closed immersion V(K^(e+1)) → X. This is scheme-theoretic annihilation, including nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 088A, construction of G_e and their adjacent quotient maps

proof.text: Unfold the flipped completion system at I-level n to formalModuleQuotient K (e+1) (M.obj.obj (op n)), and rewrite the kernel of the closed immersion using Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι.

Reuse the already-proved private power_subobject_eq and product_iso from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.ModulePullbackIdealPowerProductImage through proof-only import all. The former identifies the recursive K-power inclusion with the ideal-data power inclusion, including exponent zero; the latter transports their product images on the quotient module. Only these proved helper theorems are used, not the pullback theorem itself.

Reuse the already-proved private idealModuleProduct_quotient_zero from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentFormalModule through proof-only import all: multiplication by the recursive power on the cokernel of its product inclusion is zero. IsZero.of_iso transports this zero object across the inverse of the product isomorphism to the required ideal-data product.
